info.title: Judoscale Team API
info.description:
The Judoscale Team API gives you programmatic access to your team, apps, and processes: manage
autoscaling settings, review metrics and scaling history, and administer your team.

## Authentication

Authenticate every request with an API token, sent as a bearer token in the `Authorization`
header:

```
Authorization: Bearer jdo_...
```

Create and manage tokens in your Judoscale team account settings. A missing or invalid token
returns `401 authentication_error`.

Each token is scoped to a single team and has a **role** and an **access level**:

- **Role**: `member` or `admin`. Admin-only actions reject `member` tokens with `403 permission_error`.
- **Access**: read-only or read & write. A read-only token may only make `GET`/`HEAD` requests; any other method returns `403 permission_error`.

## Errors

The API returns conventional HTTP status codes and a consistent JSON error envelope:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "message": "...",
    "param": "id"
  }
}
```

`type` is a stable, machine-readable category; `message` is human-readable. `param` names the
offending field on validation errors.

| Status | `type` | When |
| ------ | ------ | ---- |
| 401 | `authentication_error` | Missing or invalid API token. |
| 403 | `permission_error` | A read-only token on a write request, or a non-admin token on an admin-only action. |
| 404 | `not_found` | The requested resource does not exist. |
| 422 | `invalid_request_error` | The request was malformed or failed validation. |
| 429 | `rate_limit_error` | Too many requests; the rate limit was exceeded. |
| 500 | `api_error` | An unexpected error on our end. |

## Pagination

Some list endpoints are paginated, returning up to `100` items per page. A response with more
items available includes a `next_cursor`; pass it as the `cursor` query param to fetch the
next page. Its absence means you've reached the last page.

Repeat any other filters on every request; a cursor only encodes your position in the list,
not the filters that produced it.

## Rate limits

Each API token is limited to 60 requests per minute, plus an additional per-IP limit as a
backstop against abuse. Exceeding a limit returns `429 rate_limit_error`; respect the
`Retry-After` header (seconds to wait) before retrying.

## Browser clients

The API allows cross-origin requests from any origin. A browser request that sends
`Authorization` or `Content-Type: application/json` starts with an `OPTIONS` preflight. That
preflight needs no token and does not count toward the rate limit. Send the bearer token on
the request that follows.

Responses include `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and expose `Retry-After` to browser scripts.
Do not send cookies. The API reads only the bearer token, and it does not allow credentialed
CORS requests.

get.description: The linked process, with its enabled autoscale metrics and settings.

autoscaling_enabled.description: Whether autoscaling is currently enabled on this process.

min_scale.description: The floor of the autoscaling range, in instances. `0` may be set for a worker, or a process autoscaling on `scaling_schedule`.

max_scale.description: The ceiling of the autoscaling range, in instances.

upscale_quantity.description: How many instances to add on an upscale.

upscale_interval_seconds.description: Minimum time between upscales, in seconds.

upscale_sensitivity_seconds.description: How long a metric must stay above its threshold before triggering an upscale, in seconds. Must be one of 10, 20, 30.

downscale_quantity.description: How many instances to remove on a downscale.

downscale_interval_seconds.description: Minimum time between downscales, in seconds.

sniping_enabled.description: Automatically restarts instances whose metrics stay well above the rest of the fleet. Web processes only, and only on platforms that support it.

protect_long_jobs.description: Wait for in-flight jobs to finish before scaling this worker down. Worker processes only, requires `queue_busy` metric.

all_queues.description: Autoscale on all queues instead of just the ones in `queue_names`. Worker processes only.

queue_names.description: The specific queues to autoscale on, used when `all_queues` is false. Worker processes only.

schedule_time_zone.description: The time zone schedule entries are interpreted in. Changing it shifts existing entries' time and wday by the time difference, so they keep firing at the same moment.

get.description: The metrics this process can autoscale on, which of them currently drive its autoscaling, and which have reported in the last few minutes (if applicable). Any metric listed here can be enabled, reporting or not. Only certain metrics can be combined.

autoscale_metrics.description: The metrics available to this process.

200.description: The metrics available to this process, which of them are enabled, and which have recent metrics.

patch.description:
Sets which metrics drive this process's autoscaling. What you send becomes the enabled set, so
anything left out is disabled and at least one metric is required. Thresholds are set on the
process itself.

Switching to `scaling_schedule` seeds a default schedule for a process that has none, which can
be managed through its schedule.

Switching to `response_time`, where available, creates the log drain that ingests response times
from your application logs.

metrics.description:
The metrics to autoscale on, replacing whatever is enabled today. Valid values depend on the process type and availability:
- web: `queue_time`, `utilization`, `response_time`, `scaling_schedule`
- worker: `queue_time`, `queue_depth`, `scaling_schedule`

It's possible to autoscale on multiple metrics by combining them, depending on availability:
- web:
  - `queue_time` + `utilization`
- worker:
  - `queue_depth` + `queue_time`

get.description: The process's schedule entries, ordered by day and time.

post.description: Creates the process's schedule. Omit the body to bootstrap a default one. An empty list is rejected, since a schedule needs at least one entry.

entries.description: The schedule entries to create. Omit entirely to bootstrap a default schedule.

time.description: Time of day the entry starts, in `HH:MM`, in the process's `schedule_time_zone`.

min_scale.description: The floor of the scale for this window, in instances. `0` may be set for a worker, or a process autoscaling on `scaling_schedule`.

max_scale.description: The ceiling of the scale for this window, in instances. For a process autoscaling on `scaling_schedule`, it must match `min_scale` or be left out.

put.description: Replaces the process's schedule: an entry with a matching id is updated, one without an id is created (and must give every field the same way create does), and any left out of the list are deleted.

time.description: Time of day the entry starts, in `HH:MM`, in the process's `schedule_time_zone`.

min_scale.description: The floor of the scale for this window, in instances. `0` may be set for a worker, or a process autoscaling on `scaling_schedule`.

max_scale.description: The ceiling of the scale for this window, in instances. For a process autoscaling on `scaling_schedule`, it must match `min_scale` or be left out.

id.description: An existing entry to keep. Send it alone to keep the entry as it is, or alongside the fields you want to change.

tags.name: Team
tags.description:
A team is your Judoscale account: it owns your apps and members. Most teams are billed
directly and will include their current subscription status, except for the Heroku
Add-ons where each app has its own subscription with Heroku.

tags.name: Memberships
tags.description:
A membership is a person's access to a team. Its role (member or admin) controls what
they can do.

tags.name: API Tokens
tags.description:
An API token authenticates requests to this API. Each token is scoped to a team and has a
role (member or admin) and an access level (read-only or read & write).

tags.name: Apps
tags.description:
An app is a group of processes that Judoscale monitors and autoscales. It's linked from
your platform account (Heroku, Fly, Render, etc.).

Heroku Add-on apps include their respective subscription and plan limits.

Your platform may use a different name for an "app", such as "cluster" or "project environment".

tags.name: Processes
tags.description:
A process is a component of an app, such as web or worker. Each one autoscales
independently, with its own scale range, metrics, and schedule.

Your platform may use a different name for a "process", such as "service" or "container type".

tags.name: Process Autoscale Metrics
tags.description:
Autoscale metrics drive a process's scale up or down. Examples include queue time and
utilization. This is where you see which metrics are available and which currently drive
autoscaling for a given process. Note that a scaling schedule is also considered a metric
since it drives autoscaling.

tags.name: Process Metrics
tags.description:
Metrics are the raw performance data Judoscale collects for a process. They're collected
whether or not they're used for autoscaling.

tags.name: Process Restart Events
tags.description:
A restart event is a record of Judoscale restarting a process instance. When sniping is
enabled on a process (and its platform supports it), Judoscale may restart an instance whose
metrics stay well above the rest of the fleet, to clear a stuck or degraded one. Only web
processes are eligible for restarts.

tags.name: Process Scale Events
tags.description:
A scale event is any change to a process's instance count. It can come from any source,
such as an autoscale or an external change.

tags.name: Process Schedule
tags.description:
A schedule sets a process's scale for specific days and times. It lets the process
autoscale differently (or not at all) on a fixed calendar.

For a process autoscaling on `scaling_schedule`, an entry's `min_scale` and `max_scale` are
always equal, since the schedule is the process's only scale signal; otherwise they set the
autoscaling range for that window.

Each entry's `time` is interpreted in the process's `schedule_time_zone`. Changing that time
zone shifts every entry's `time` and `wday` to keep firing at the same moment.

ApiToken.description: Team API token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer jdo_...`.

label.description: Names the token so you can tell your tokens apart. Must be unique within the team.

role.description: An admin token can manage the team and who belongs to it.

read_only.description: A read-only token may only make GET requests.

last_used_on.description: The last date this token was used, or null if it never has been.

App.description: A linked application Judoscale monitors and autoscales.

name.description: Synced from the platform, can't be changed.

maintenance_enabled_at.description: When maintenance mode was enabled, or null if it's off.

webhook_url.description: Where Judoscale posts scaling notifications for this app, or null if none is set.

subscription.description: The add-on subscription for this app. Null when Judoscale bills the team directly, in which case the subscription belongs to the team instead.

AutoscaleMetric.description: A metric this process autoscales on. Thresholds are omitted for `scaling_schedule`, which scales on the schedule rather than a measured value.

metric.description:
Valid values depend on the process type:
- web: `queue_time`, `utilization`, `response_time`, `scaling_schedule`
- worker: `queue_time`, `queue_depth`, `scaling_schedule`

upscale_threshold.description: The value above which this metric triggers an upscale, in the metric's own unit (see the metrics endpoint).

downscale_threshold.description: The value below which this metric triggers a downscale, in the metric's own unit (see the metrics endpoint).

AutoscaleMetricStatus.description: A metric's availability and autoscaling state for a process.

metric.description: Only the metrics that apply to this process type are listed.

enabled.description: Whether this metric currently drives the process's autoscaling.

has_recent_metrics.description: Whether the process has reported this metric in the last few minutes. Null for anything that doesn't have metrics, such as a scaling schedule. A metric can be enabled without reporting.

Membership.description: A person's access to a team.

role.description: Admins can manage the team and who belongs to it.

invitation_pending.description: They have been invited but haven't signed up yet.

otp_status.description: Whether they have two-factor authentication enabled. Members who sign in through SSO cannot set it up.

synced.description: True when this membership is synced from the team's platform (e.g. Heroku) and can't be changed directly.

Metric.description: A metric Judoscale can report for a process.

metric.description:
Valid values depend on the process type:
- web: `queue_time`, `utilization`, `response_time`, `rps`
- worker: `queue_time`, `queue_depth`, `queue_busy`

unit.description: How the metric's values are measured.

MetricSeries.description: A metric's data points over a time window.

metric.description:
Valid values depend on the process type:
- web: `queue_time`, `utilization`, `response_time`, `rps`
- worker: `queue_time`, `queue_depth`, `queue_busy`

unit.description: How the metric's values are measured.

bucket_width_seconds.description: Width of each bucket, in seconds, determined by the time window.

points.description: One data point per bucket, oldest first. A bucket with no reported data has a value of 0.

MetricSeriesPerInstance.description: A metric's data points over a time window, split by instance.

unit.description: How the metric's values are measured.

bucket_width_seconds.description: Width of each bucket, in seconds, determined by the time window.

instances.description: One entry per instance, each covering the same buckets.

instance.description: The platform's identifier for the instance, such as `web.1`.

Process.description: A component of an app, such as web or worker, that autoscales independently.

name.description: Synced from the platform, can't be changed.

autoscaling_enabled.description: Whether autoscaling is currently enabled on this process.

min_scale.description: The floor of the autoscaling range, in instances. `0` may be set for a worker, or a process autoscaling on `scaling_schedule`.

max_scale.description: The ceiling of the autoscaling range, in instances.

upscale_quantity.description: How many instances to add on an upscale.

upscale_interval_seconds.description: Minimum time between upscales, in seconds.

upscale_sensitivity_seconds.description: How long a metric must stay above its threshold before triggering an upscale, in seconds. Must be one of 10, 20, 30.

downscale_quantity.description: How many instances to remove on a downscale.

downscale_interval_seconds.description: Minimum time between downscales, in seconds.

schedule_time_zone.description: The time zone schedule entries are interpreted in. Changing it shifts existing entries' time and wday by the time difference, so they keep firing at the same moment.

autoscale_metrics.description: The metrics currently driving this process's autoscaling. Empty means the process still needs setup.

sniping_enabled.description: Automatically restarts instances whose metrics stay well above the rest of the fleet. Web processes only, and only on platforms that support it.

protect_long_jobs.description: Wait for in-flight jobs to finish before scaling this worker down. Worker processes only, requires `queue_busy` metric.

all_queues.description: Autoscale on all queues instead of just the ones in `queue_names`. Worker processes only.

queue_names.description: The specific queues to autoscale on, used when `all_queues` is false. Worker processes only.

RestartEvent.description: A record of an instance Judoscale restarted.

instance.description: The platform's identifier for the restarted instance, such as `web.1`.

ScaleEvent.description: A change to a process's instance count.

previous_scale.description: The instance count before this event.

new_scale.description: The instance count after this event.

scale_direction.description: Null when the scale did not change.

source.description: `autoscale` when Judoscale changed the scale, `external` when it changed outside Judoscale (e.g. the platform dashboard or CLI), or `maintenance` when maintenance mode changed it.

ScheduleEntry.description: A day, time, and scale for a process to autoscale on.

time.description: Time of day the entry starts, in `HH:MM`, in the process's `schedule_time_zone`.

min_scale.description: The floor of the scale for this window, in instances. `0` may be set for a worker, or a process autoscaling on `scaling_schedule`.

max_scale.description: The ceiling of the scale for this window, in instances. Equals `min_scale` for a process autoscaling on `scaling_schedule`.

Subscription.description: A billing plan, its status, and its limits.

plan.description: The plan's display name, e.g. "Orange Belt".

legacy.description: This plan is no longer offered for new subscriptions.

status.description: Anything other than `active` means the last payment did not go through.

limits.description: How far the plan allows scaling. Null means no limit, and a `max_perf_scale` of 0 means the plan has no performance instances.

autoscale_events.description: Autoscales allowed per month, and how many are left. Null on plans that do not meter them.

Team.description: Your Judoscale account: owns your apps and members.

otp_required.description: Whether members must set up two-factor authentication to sign in.

subscription.description: The team's subscription, when Judoscale bills the team directly. Null for add-on customers, whose subscription belongs to each app instead.

param.description: The offending parameter, for validation errors.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests; the rate limit was exceeded.

Forbidden.description: The token lacks permission for this action.

NotFound.description: The requested resource does not exist.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The request was malformed or failed validation.

InternalServerError.description: An unexpected error occurred on our end.
